cur-fossil-ediacara.dateNote: In 1946 the geologist Reg Sprigg found soft-bodied fossils in these South Australian hills. They are about 555 million years old — older than the Cambrian, and among the first large living things.

cur-fossil-alcoota.dateNote: In 1962 fossil bones were found on Alcoota Station, north-east of Alice Springs. Digs since have found thousands of bones, among them the giant flightless bird Dromornis stirtoni, one of the biggest birds ever. They are about 8 million years old (Late Miocene).
cur-fossil-alcoota.summary: A bonebed in central Australia with one of the biggest birds that ever lived.
